instruction: Send the following phone message to my roommates and friends, who do not have a venmo account, "Make an account on venmo please.".
notes: The actual contact book is unknown, so the problem encodes a representative world: two roommates and two friends, of which roommate-a and friend-b already have Venmo accounts (static world fact has-venmo-account) and roommate-b and friend-a do not. Knowledge flow: supervisor.show_profile yields the phone username (phone_number) and venmo username (email); show_account_passwords yields passwords; phone.search_contacts is called once per relationship (query and relationship both set to the relation name) and marks (contacts-searched ?r), which unlocks the statically stored email/phone of every contact with that relationship; venmo.show_profile on a contact's email marks (venmo-status-known ?p) (in the real API a missing account is signalled by an error message); phone.send_text_message is only allowed for contacts whose status has been checked and who have no Venmo account, and never twice to the same contact. Because STRIPS has no quantified goals, the number of required recipients is tracked by a unary counter (remaining count-N decremented by each send through count-succ); count-0 is a domain constant so that supervisor-complete-task can require (remaining count-0) without extra parameters, which under the model is equivalent to 'every roommate/friend without Venmo has been messaged exactly once'. The goal additionally lists the explicit message-sent facts and venmo-status-known for all contacts so the reference plan checks every contact, as a real agent must. venmo.login is done once (the reference solution needlessly re-logs in per contact). complete_task carries no answer since the task is not a question.

plan: (phone-send-text-message phone-friend-a msg-make-an-account-on-venmo-please phone-token friend-a count-1 count-2)
(phone-send-text-message phone-roommate-b msg-make-an-account-on-venmo-please phone-token roommate-b count-0 count-1)
